reports.title: Anxiety and Mood Disturbance Are Prospectively Associated With Respiratory Infection Risk and the Mucosal Immune Response to Exercise
reports.authors: Harrison SE; Edwards JP; Roberts R; Walsh NP
source_locator: Full text PMC12480926; European Journal of Sport Science 2025;25:e70058
reports.inclusion_reason: Two sub-studies, each a single identifiable bout: Study 1 = field marathon with pre/immediate-post saliva; Study 2 = lab 60-min treadmill run at 65% VO2peak with pre/post/+30min saliva and a seated-rest comparator. Both adult cohorts, direct mucosal immune marker (SIgA).
reports.reviewer_notes: Charting-only pilot; no screening workbook consulted. Report contains two cohorts/designs (field + lab); see study_families/cohorts split and unresolved_questions.
reports.author_stated_use: Monitoring mucosal immune health (SIgA) in relation to psychological stress/anxiety/mood around exercise, with a recommendation that athletes manage psychological well-being and that researchers account for psychological factors in exercise-immunology study design; not framed as a standalone diagnostic/predictive marker use.
author_window_interpretation_locator: p.1 Introduction: 'showing greater risk of respiratory infection after marathon and ultramarathon events'

precision_validation.evidence_notes: Explicit intra-assay CV reported for the SIgA ELISA (2.9% Study 1). Outlier-removal and CV>15% exclusion criteria reported.

precision_validation.response_evidence: Two timepoints only: pre-race and immediately post-race
source_locator: p.3 Methods 2.1.2: 'Saliva samples were collected prior to and immediately after the marathon'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Bins used: pre_exercise_baseline and 0_to_lt30min (immediate post). No recovery/outside-window sampling; no exact finish-to-sample interval reported per runner (field logistics).

source_locator: p.5 Methods 2.4: SIgA measured by ELISA, the most common mucosal antibody
precision_validation.evidence_notes: SIgA is a direct, recognised mucosal immune mediator.

precision_validation.individualization: Response heterogeneity in SIgA SR partly explained by trait anxiety and TMD (Table 3: trait anxiety p=0.010, TMD p=0.011); no repeated-baseline or ICC/CV of the biological response itself.
source_locator: p.6 Table 3 and Results 3.1.2: trait anxiety and TMD associated with greater reduction in saliva SIgA SR
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Evidence of inter-individual variability sources (psychological moderators) but not a repeated-baseline/reproducibility design; single pre-post measurement per person.

precision_validation.temporal_order: Saliva sampled pre- and immediately post-marathon; RTI monitored via Jackson common-cold questionnaire for 2 weeks before and after, i.e. markers measured before most RTI onsets
source_locator: p.6 Results 3.1.3: 'no association between saliva flow rate, SIgA concentration or SIgA SR change...and RTI...OR [95% CI] 1.00...1.00...1.00 [0.97-1.01]; p>0.05'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Pilot-purpose finding: explicit null association between the mucosal immune (SIgA) response to the marathon and subsequent respiratory infection risk (M-R56-04). Trait anxiety/TMD (non-immune, psychological variables) DID predict RTI risk directly (Table 2), but that is not an immune-marker-to-outcome association.

precision_validation.replication: No replication cohort for Study 1 findings
source_locator: p.7 Discussion: 'further research should examine interventions to reduce anxiety and improve mood prior to exercise'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: No external cohort replication; Study 2 is an independent mechanistic laboratory follow-up of the SAME research group, not an external validation cohort for Study 1's RTI finding.

precision_validation.field_feasibility: Non-invasive swab-based saliva collection feasible at marathon-registration/race-day scale (406 recruited, 210 final SIgA sample) without laboratory infrastructure on site
source_locator: p.3 Methods 2.1.2: field collection via Versi-SAL swab; p.3 Figure 1 flow chart
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Feasible field deployment demonstrated at moderate scale; substantial data loss (49% of saliva-eligible participants) is itself feasibility-relevant.

source_locator: p.5 Methods 2.4: 'Mean intra-assay CVs for sample duplicates were 2.9% and 3.3% for Study 1 and Study 2, respectively'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Explicit intra-assay CV (3.3%) for Study 2 SIgA ELISA; controlled lab conditions (temperature, humidity, fasting, hydration standardised).

precision_validation.response_evidence: Three timepoints: pre, immediate post, +30 min post, for both EX and CON

precision_validation.evidence_notes: Bins used: pre_exercise_baseline, 0_to_lt30min, 30min_to_lt3h (EX) and matched_control_time (CON). No sampling beyond 30 min post; no outside-window recovery sample.

source_locator: p.5 Methods 2.4

precision_validation.individualization: Sex-specific response: negative correlations between trait/state anxiety, TMD, perceived stress and SIgA SR response found in men (r=-0.55 to -0.68, p<0.01) but not replicated in women (mixed findings); within-subject crossover design controls for between-person confounding.
source_locator: p.7 Figure 3 and Results 3.2.1: 'trait anxiety: r=-0.59**... Perceived psychological stress: r=-0.68**' (men); p.7 'did not replicate this relationship in women'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Clear demonstration of response heterogeneity by sex; no repeated-baseline/ICC of the SIgA response itself across repeated non-exercise days.

extraction_provenance.provenance_notes: AI-only charting pilot run; all eligibility/extraction values provisional.

eligibility_opinion.rationale: Both sub-studies describe a single identifiable bout with a pre-bout baseline and >=1 post-bout immune sample in adults: Study 1 is the 2017 Snowdonia Marathon (p.2 'n=406 adults...completed the 2017 Snowdonia Marathon'); Study 2 is a 60-min treadmill bout at 65% VO2peak with a seated-rest comparator (p.3 '60 min of continuous treadmill running at 65% VO2peak...or remained seated'). Neither sub-study tracks the same marker across >=2 identified exercise bouts in the same people, so Support B does not apply; the CON arm of Study 2 is a non-exercise comparator, not a second bout.

unresolved_questions: Saliva flow rate (FR) is listed in the dictionary under sample_sets.normalization, yet this paper treats FR as a primary mucosal-immune-response outcome and formally tests it against RTI risk (Table 2-equivalent OR analysis). Charted FR as its own measurement row with marker_family='other' rather than only as a normalization field; needs team guidance on whether FR should ever be a chartable 'marker' row.

report_cohort_links.n_analyzed is a single integer, but Study 1 has three different analytic denominators depending on outcome (RTI-only n=336, SIgA-only n=210, combined n=199); used n=210 (the immune-marker-relevant sample) and documented the others in link_notes -- the schema does not cleanly support multiple denominators per link.

Study 2's CON (seated-rest) arm readings were coded sample_role='nonexercise_control' / time_bin='matched_control_time' even though CON has its own internal pre/post/+30min structure mirroring EX; unclear whether CON timepoints should instead get their own bout_id or be modelled only as a comparator attached to the EX sample_sets.

Table 3 / Figure 3 psychological-moderator correlations (trait anxiety, TMD, perceived stress vs SIgA response) were charted as precision_validation.individualization evidence rather than as separate measurement rows, since psychological stress is not among the manual's named example covariates (only cortisol/CK/lactate/HRV); flagging this classification choice for review.

Study 1 and Study 2 were split into two separate study_families (different designs, different populations, different locations) sharing one report; the manual supports this ('study family是独立研究'), but the two sub-studies are run by the same authors as parts of one paper, so the team may prefer one study_family with two cohorts -- flagged as a row-unit calibration question.

Study 1's exact post-marathon sample timing relative to each runner's own finish is not reported (only clock-time averages for a field with staggered finish times spanning ~2.5-5h); time_bin 0_to_lt30min for the post sample is an interpretation of 'immediately after', not a verified per-runner interval.
